answer: Divergent history challenge. Each identity must harbor a private random seed and publish a hash chain over its own past actions; clones forced to share state cannot produce two chains that later reconcile without a collision. A challenger requests a fresh branch point, and any fork that a clone cannot resolve reveals the duplicate, letting honest nodes garden distinct lineage records. The attacker must run and maintain separate authentic histories per identity, paying full compute and storage per clone rather than one shared meadow of state.
